title: Checkpoint 5: Lucky Numbers Pipeline
hints: Three higher-order functions, one after another.
`filter` keeps odd numbers, `sorted()` orders them, `map` builds strings.
jsBridge: JS `arr.filter().sort().map()` becomes Swift's `filter { }.sorted().map { }`, almost identical. Two differences: `sorted()` returns a new array (JS `sort` mutates), and the default sort is numeric, not JS's lexicographic `[10, 9].sort()` surprise.

compass.q: `[10, 9, 1].sort()` in JS gives `[1, 10, 9]`. What does Swift's `sorted()` do, and why?
Chained `filter`/`map` creates intermediate arrays. When would you use `.lazy`?
Chains like this often live in view models for display lists. When should they be precomputed instead of recomputed in `body`?
Java Streams are lazy by default and need `.collect()`. Swift's are eager unless you ask for `lazy`. Which default is better?
